newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says Africa crude shipment one-time sale.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says Africa crude shipment one-time sale.

text.p: Mexico's sale of about 30,700 barrels per day (bpd) of crude to South Africa in May was a one-time deal with client Texaco Inc., a Pemex crude trader said on Friday.

"Texaco asked us to send the volume to South Africa," the trader, who declined to be named, told Reuters. "It is not necessarily a regular transaction but could happen again with Texaco if the conditions and price are right."
State oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said on Friday it exported crude to Africa for the first time in its history.
"For the first time part of export volumes was sent to the African continent (two percent)," Pemex said.
It did not say at what price or what type of crude was sold.
Pemex only sells crude through contracts to established clients with refineries.
